body:
REVISED RENDERER PLAN AFTER READING INTAGLIO, SUPERSEDING MY V3. My prior plan treated deck.gl as a direct StoryAtlas lowering beside Intaglio. The measured seam is more useful than that.

At the StoryAtlas pin 596b398, Intaglio already has a renderer-neutral `Scene` that resolves to `DeviceScene`: discs, polylines, compound polygons, rectangles, text, images, ordered groups, clipping, rotation, style, and optional `GraphicsName`. It already ships SVG, Scala.js Canvas 2D, Java2D, and JavaFX backends plus a shared `RendererConformance` court. StoryAtlas currently consumes only core plus SVG and directly injects SVG DOM. It has not yet dogfooded the existing Canvas backend.

The limit is equally concrete. Intaglio has no generic picking or hit-test result, camera, viewport-driven tile provider, semantic zoom or LOD loader, interaction state, backend capability outcome, or accessibility twin. `GraphicsName` is only a nonblank string and is not globally unique by contract. Scalar fields and contours compile to ordinary 2D primitives; there is no retained 2.5D terrain or tile-pyramid semantic. StoryAtlas names mark groups, often leaving their child primitives unnamed, so interactive picking needs an explicit nearest-owned-name or pick-index law rather than assuming DOM `data-name`. Local Intaglio is two commits ahead of the StoryAtlas pin and has additional dirty pattern-tile work; none of that is a consumable dependency until separately reviewed, landed, and pinned.

Therefore use this sequence.

1. FIRST BACKEND SPIKE: lower the exact same O3, dense-feature, and high-mark-count scenes once to Intaglio `DeviceScene`, then compare existing SVG and existing Canvas 2D. This is the cheapest honest dogfood court. Require primitive and group identity, clipping and z-order, pattern/status support or explicit Unsupported, deterministic command output, selection-index construction, direct-file opening, textual twin, and named frame-time, memory, and bundle-size evidence. Canvas becomes preferred for a workload only if it wins the predeclared gate.

2. IF THAT GATE MISSES, split deck.gl work by abstraction. A generic primitive renderer from `DeviceScene` to deck.gl layers can be proposed to Intaglio as an optional `intaglio-deckgl` Scala.js backend and must pass Intaglio renderer conformance. StoryAtlas still owns camera and focus, viewport tile and LOD requests, stale-result rejection, semantic pick-to-address resolution, requested-layer accounting, and accessibility. Do not widen Intaglio with story semantics or an unproven interaction framework.

3. Keep any StoryAtlas interaction or tile host internal and removable until a second non-story consumer demonstrates the abstraction. Only then consider extracting a general module. This meets the lift-out goal without designing a generic library from one client.

4. Controlled 2.5D terrain is not backend parity with the current `DeviceScene`. Admit it as a separately declared capability and specialization, with a 2D track or contour twin and explicit Unsupported on backends that cannot preserve it.

This correction narrows rather than expands authority: no dependency, code, pin update, Intaglio edit, module name, or performance claim is authorized. Chief should route the SVG-versus-Canvas court before any deck.gl dependency decision, unless the durable O3 packet exposes a capability that Canvas cannot represent by construction.
